Title: Maximizing Own VP = Minimizing Others VP ?

Messages.Author: Johannes Walch
Messages.Body:
Hi,

in our last tournament yesterday a rather difficult question/situation
arose. We have played a 4 player table with Me, Player A, Player B, Player
C. Me and B have (both playing vote decks) have cooperated through the whole
game by voting with each other all (!) the time, because Player C was also
playing a vote deck AND we would have been able to shut us down because we
were both relying on Voter Captivations.

After about 2 hourse the game was approaching the time limit with no one
ousted. It was my turn, my prey (Player A) had 3 pool I had only 1 vampire
open and this vampire was calling a Kine Resources Contested, which would
oust A and giving me 1,5 VP and B,C 0,5 VP instead of 0,5 VP for everyone.
Player B愀 first idea was to vote with me, because we were cooperating the
whole game and the quite "out of game" time limit thing has nothing to do
with it. But the judge said no you are not allowed to vote with him because
you have to play to max your VPs. I argued against, that we had some kind of
deal AND he was maximizing his VPs he was just not minimizing mine.

In the end it didn愒 matter because I was in the final anyway, but how
should the judge decide in such a situation ? I have collected all the
arguments for both sides, but I want to hear your opinion first. Thats
probably less biased then :-)

johannes walch

Messages.Author: Johannes Walch
Messages.Body:
> Player B愀 first idea was to vote with me, because we were cooperating the
> whole game and the quite "out of game" time limit thing has nothing to do
> with it.

I have to add that I even discarded an Awe and a Bewitching Oration (which
together would have made me pass the vote on my own) 2 and 3 turns before,
because I was never thinking of the possibility that he might not be allowed
to vote with me !

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


B can vote with you so long as doing so doesn't reduce B's prospect of a
Game Win, or, if he cannot get a GW, doesn't reduce his expected VP tally.

Messages.Author: Joscha Duell
Messages.Body:
LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3E75E594...@white-wolf.com>...

> B can vote with you so long as doing so doesn't reduce B's prospect of a
> Game Win, or, if he cannot get a GW, doesn't reduce his expected VP tally.

How can I maximise my VPs if I give one away freely without a valid
deal? It was short before timeout, Player B couldn't expect to get
help from Johannes for his kill because there was no time left for
that. For what reason should he help someone to make a kill if he does
not get something in return. Just because of loyalty for the help he
got in the turns before? I think not, because both players had a
benefit of their support, so nobody owed something to the other player
(caution: bad englisch).

I think, this problem is a question of style. I don't think, you can
rule that perfectly. In my opinion Johannes and Player B should have
make a clear deal before. I was the player to be ousted and I didn't
called the judge. But I questioned Player B why he wanted to throw
away a VP for nothing. I don't help somebody to get a VP and 6 blood,
something what could mean a place in the Finals, just because of
sympathy, do I?

Messages.Body:
Joscha Duell wrote:
> LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3E75E594...@white-wolf.com>...
>
>>B can vote with you so long as doing so doesn't reduce B's prospect of a
>>Game Win, or, if he cannot get a GW, doesn't reduce his expected VP tally.
>
>
> How can I maximise my VPs if I give one away freely without a valid
> deal?

If your expected VP accumulation is 0 with or without the "deal" (which is
not the right term here, since there's no actual deal), then you are free
to go ahead with the deal or go ahead without the deal.

> It was short before timeout, Player B couldn't expect to get
> help from Johannes for his kill because there was no time left for
> that. For what reason should he help someone to make a kill if he does
> not get something in return.

If you can't help yourself, every action you take (or omit) will help one
player or another (or will be immaterial).

> Just because of loyalty for the help he
> got in the turns before? I think not, because both players had a
> benefit of their support, so nobody owed something to the other player
> (caution: bad englisch).

"Owed" hasn't been part of the argument or the answer so far.

> I think, this problem is a question of style. I don't think, you can
> rule that perfectly. In my opinion Johannes and Player B should have
> make a clear deal before. I was the player to be ousted and I didn't
> called the judge. But I questioned Player B why he wanted to throw
> away a VP for nothing. I don't help somebody to get a VP and 6 blood,
> something what could mean a place in the Finals, just because of
> sympathy, do I?

B didn't have the VP. So he's not throwing it away.
If his action resulted in him taking 1 fewer VP than he would have
otherwise received, *then* he would be "throwing away" a VP.
But that isn't how the situation was described.


